justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have retained the R4 maxValueSet extension alongside binding.additional for maximum bindings, but only as duplicate legacy metadata.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Dual representation would help older StructureDefinition tooling but creates synchronization risk and could prolong reliance on a deprecated extension pattern.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: a formerly extension-based maximum binding became part of the core `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` model while preserving the same primary and maximum value-set URLs. This is not a Distance instance-shape break, and the impact is limited to validators, code generators, and conversion tooling that read raw StructureDefinition metadata. A less-breaking base design was possible, but it would have required keeping the old extension in parallel with the new first-class field, so the remaining breakage is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have emitted both `binding.additional[{purpose: "maximum"}]` and the old `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension for this maximum binding. That would preserve most R4-era metadata consumers while still introducing the R6 core representation. The alternative is only partial because it duplicates the same conformance fact, requires the two representations to stay synchronized, does not cover the richer R6 additional-binding model beyond the legacy maximum-binding case, and risks legacy extension use accumulating indefinitely instead of disappearing.
